Map diversity as a continuous surface, with its uncertainty

geo_diversity_surface.Rd

geo_diversity_surface() turns a community table (sites x species counts) into continuous maps of Hill-number diversity:

  1. For every site it estimates diversity of order q (0 = richness, 1 = exponential Shannon, 2 = inverse Simpson) at a common sample coverage with tidydiversity::div_standardise() (Chao and Jost 2012), so sites sampled with different effort are compared fairly. The bootstrap standard error of each estimate is kept.

  2. It interpolates each q by ordinary kriging with measurement error (Cressie 1993): each site's estimation variance is added to the kriging system, so poorly sampled, uncertain sites count for less and the map shows the underlying diversity surface rather than sampling noise. The variogram nugget is filtered the same way, so the surface is smooth through the sites. Kriging runs on the log scale (diversity is positive and right-skewed) in C++ on several cores.

  3. It returns, for each q, the predicted diversity and a 95% interval, whose width combines spatial uncertainty (distance from sampled sites) and estimation uncertainty (how well each site was sampled).

The variogram of each q is fitted with gstat unless you give one. Coverage-based standardisation, Hill numbers and kriging with known measurement error each exist on their own; this function links them so a diversity map carries an honest uncertainty map.

Usage

geo_diversity_surface(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  sites,
  lon = lon,
  lat = lat,
  crs = 4326,
  q = c(0, 1, 2),
  coverage = NULL,
  grid = 100,
  model = c("Exp", "Sph", "Gau"),
  measurement_error = TRUE,
  nboot = 50,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

Long community table: one row per species per site.

site, species, abundance

<data-masking> Columns for site, species and counts (abundance = NULL counts rows).

sites

Site locations: an sf point table, or a data frame with longitude/latitude (or x/y) columns, with a column named like site in data.

lon, lat

<data-masking> Coordinate columns when sites is not sf.

crs

CRS of lon/lat when sites is not sf (default WGS 84).

q

Orders of diversity.

coverage

Sample coverage to standardise to. NULL uses the tidydiversity default (the highest coverage reachable by all sites without extrapolating beyond twice the smallest sample).

grid

Where to predict: a terra::SpatRaster template, or the number of cells along the longer side of the sites' extent (default 100).

model

Variogram model: "Exp", "Sph" or "Gau".

measurement_error

Use each site's estimation variance in the kriging (recommended)? FALSE gives ordinary kriging.

nboot

Bootstrap replicates for the site standard errors.

level

Width of the prediction interval.

Value

A SpatRaster with three layers per q: q0 (predicted diversity, the back-transformed log-scale prediction), q0_lower and q0_upper (interval bounds), and so on. Attribute "sites" holds the per-site estimates, standard errors and coordinates; "variograms" holds the fitted variogram of each q.

References

Chao, A. and Jost, L. (2012). Coverage-based rarefaction and extrapolation. Ecology, 93, 2533-2547. doi:10.1890/11-1952.1

Cressie, N. (1993). Statistics for Spatial Data, revised edition. Wiley. doi:10.1002/9781119115151

See also

plot_diversity_surface(), geo_interpolate()

Examples

# Trees in 50 one-hectare plots of the Barro Colorado Island forest
# dynamics plot, Panama (Condit et al. 2002; shipped with vegan)
e <- new.env()
utils::data(BCI, BCI.env, package = "vegan", envir = e)
trees <- tibble::tibble(
  plot = rep(sprintf("P%02d", 1:50), ncol(e$BCI)),
  species = rep(colnames(e$BCI), each = 50),
  n = as.vector(as.matrix(e$BCI))
)
trees <- trees[trees$n > 0, ]
plots <- tibble::tibble(
  plot = sprintf("P%02d", 1:50),
  x = e$BCI.env$UTM.EW, y = e$BCI.env$UTM.NS
)
set.seed(1)
surf <- geo_diversity_surface(trees, plot, species, n,
  sites = plots, lon = x, lat = y, crs = 32617, grid = 40, nboot = 20
)
surf
